# VGC Team Report

Updated: 2026-08-03
Source: https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com

> VGC Team Report is the premier team report builder and sharing platform for competitive Pokémon Video Game Championship (VGC) players. Unlike paste viewers (PokePaste) or usage-statistics tools (Pikalytics), VGC Team Report lets players author rich, structured team reports with damage calculations, matchup plans, speed tier breakdowns, and strategy notes — then share them as a permanent public link or embed them anywhere.

## What makes it different from other tools

**PokePaste** (`pokepast.es`) is a plain-text paste bin for Showdown-format team data. It shows moves, items, EVs, and natures in raw text — nothing more. It has no strategy sections, no damage calculations, no matchup analysis, and no community browsing features.

**Pikalytics** (`pikalytics.com`) aggregates usage statistics and rental team data to show which Pokémon and moves are most popular at a given rating range. It is a meta-analysis tool, not a team report tool. It doesn't let players document *why* they made specific build choices or how to play their team.

**VGC Team Report** bridges the gap: import a Showdown paste, then author a complete team report with per-Pokémon strategy notes, EV justifications, damage calculations against relevant threats, speed tier comparisons, and matchup plans. The finished report is shareable via a short link and embeddable in any website or Discord.

## Main URLs

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/
The homepage and primary entry point. Visitors can:
- Paste Showdown-format team text directly or paste a pokepast.es URL to import a team
- Click "Analyze" to generate an auto-populated report skeleton
- Fill in strategy notes, matchup plans, damage calcs, and speed comparisons
- Share or publish the completed report

No account is required to build or view a report. Creating a free account unlocks saving multiple reports, version history, and real-time collaboration with teammates.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/explore
The community explore feed. All public reports appear here. Visitors can filter by:
- Format / regulation set (Reg G, Reg H, Champions Reg M-A, Champions Reg M-B, etc.)
- Specific Pokémon (e.g. "show me all reports that run Calyrex-Ice")
- Tournament (e.g. "top teams from 2025 Worlds")
- Player name or creator handle

This is the primary discovery surface for players researching a new meta or preparing for an upcoming event.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/tournaments
Tournament archive. Curated collection of team reports from top finishers at official Pokémon VGC events:
- World Championships (annual, highest prestige)
- International Championships (NAIC, EUIC, LAIC — three per season)
- Regional Championships (multiple per season, across North America, Europe, Latin America, Oceania)
- Online tournaments (Global Challenge, etc.)

Each tournament card shows the event name, date, location, format, number of team reports, and the most-used Pokémon in the field.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/champions
Dedicated hub for the Pokémon Champions formats (Regulation M-A and Regulation M-B). Covers:
- What the Champions format is and how it differs from standard VGC
- Featured team reports in the Champions format
- Commonly used Mega Evolutions and restricted legendaries in the format
- An index linking to a guide page for every sprited Mega Evolution

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/champions/[mega]
Per-Mega guide pages, one for every Mega Evolution that is legal in Regulation M-B (a superset of M-A) and has a Pokémon Showdown sprite — for example `/champions/metagross-mega`, `/champions/blaziken-mega`, `/champions/swampert-mega`, `/champions/mawile-mega`. Each page shows the Mega's typing, ability, required Mega Stone, and full base stat line, then lists public team reports on this site that run it.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/faq
Answers to common questions about the platform, team reports, VGC formats, importing teams, and sharing reports. See the FAQ section below for a summary.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/changelog
Running log of product updates: new features, format support additions, bug fixes, and performance improvements.

### https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/s/[id]
Individual team report pages. Each public report is accessible at a permanent short URL of this form. These pages include full JSON-LD structured data and Open Graph tags for rich previews when shared on social media or Discord.

## FAQ

### What is the Champions format?

Pokémon Champions is a VGC format introduced for the 2026 competitive season, first as **Regulation M-A** and then as **Regulation M-B**. It reintroduces Mega Evolutions — a mechanic last seen in standard competitive play in Generation 6/7 — alongside the modern Pokémon Scarlet & Violet roster.

Key rules (identical across Reg M-A and Reg M-B):
- Teams of 6, bring 4 to battle (standard VGC doubles format)
- Up to two restricted Legendary Pokémon are allowed (same limit as Regulation G/H)
- Mega Evolutions are legal — one Pokémon per team can Mega Evolve in battle
- Stats are trained with **SP (Stat Points): 66 total per Pokémon, 32 maximum in any one stat** — not with EVs. See "What is the difference between SP and EVs?" below.
- IVs are locked to 31 in every stat
- **Terastallization is not available** in Champions

The format creates a dramatically different meta from previous regulation sets because Mega Evolutions bypass the standard Ability system while active, enabling combinations not seen in recent VGC history (e.g., Mega Kangaskhan's Parental Bond, Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost, Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag).

### What is the difference between Regulation M-A and Regulation M-B?

**Regulation M-B is a strict superset of Regulation M-A.** Every Pokémon and every Mega Evolution legal in M-A is also legal in M-B; M-B then adds further base-form Pokémon and 16 additional Mega Evolutions. The reverse is not true — an M-B-only pick is illegal in M-A.

Megas that are legal in Reg M-B but not Reg M-A include Mega Sceptile, Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert, Mega Mawile, Mega Metagross, Mega Raichu X, Mega Raichu Y, Mega Staraptor, Mega Scolipede, Mega Scrafty, Mega Eelektross, Mega Pyroar, Mega Malamar, Mega Barbaracle, Mega Dragalge and Mega Falinks.

**Regulation M-B is the current format**, and is the format used at the 2026 Pokémon World Championships.

VGC Team Report supports both Champions regulations fully: import a team with Mega Stones, build your report, filter the Explore page by either format, and read per-Mega guides at `/champions/[mega]` for every sprited M-A and M-B legal Mega Evolution.

### How do I share a team report?

1. Build your team report on the homepage (or open an existing saved report).
2. Click the **Share** button in the top navigation bar.
3. Choose **Publish** to make the report publicly visible on the Explore page and give it a permanent link at `https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/s/[id]`.
4. Alternatively, use **Copy Link** to get a direct URL without publishing to the public feed.
5. Use **Embed** to get an `<iframe>` snippet for embedding the report in a team page, tournament article, or website.

Shared reports are read-only for visitors. The owner (or collaborators with the edit link) can continue making changes — the public link always reflects the latest saved version.

### What is the difference between SP and EVs?

They are two different stat-training systems belonging to two different games, with two different budgets. **SP is not a notation for EVs, and 1 SP does not equal 1 EV.**

**EVs (Effort Values)** are the Scarlet & Violet-era mechanic. Each Pokémon can hold a maximum of **508 total EVs, with a cap of 252 in any single stat**. 4 EVs = 1 stat point at level 50 (for most stats). EVs are what Pokémon Showdown format and PokePaste use, and what standard VGC regulations (Reg G, Reg H, Reg I) are built on.

**SP (Stat Points)** is the stat-training system in **Pokémon Champions**, used by Regulation M-A and Regulation M-B. The budget is **66 SP in total per Pokémon, with a maximum of 32 SP in any single stat**. There is no 252, and there is no 508. Because the two budgets differ by roughly an order of magnitude, a spread like `22 HP / 11 Def / 24 SpA / 4 SpD / 5 Spe` (66 SP, a fully-invested Champions Pokémon) means something entirely different from the same numbers read as EVs (66 EVs, an almost completely untrained Pokémon).

**How VGC Team Report handles both.** Pokémon Showdown has no `SPs:` line yet, so Champions teams carry SP values inside the `EVs:` line. The importer detects this: if every value in a spread fits within [0, 32] **and** the values total at most 66, the only consistent reading is "these are already SP", and they pass through unconverted.

If a team is genuinely pasted in EV form but tagged as a Champions format, the report converts it proportionally to what was actually invested — approximately 252 EVs → 32 SP (full investment), 4 EVs → 1 SP (minimum investment), 0 EVs → 0 SP — then caps each stat at 32 SP and the whole spread at 66 SP. Any leftover budget is deliberately left unspent rather than redistributed, so the report never invents investment the author did not make. This is a display convenience for imported EV spreads; **it is not an in-game exchange rate between the two systems.**

### How do I embed a team report?

After publishing a report (see "How do I share a team report?" above):

1. Click **Share** → **Embed**.
2. Copy the `<iframe>` code provided.
3. Paste it into any HTML page, website builder, or CMS that supports raw HTML embeds.

The embed renders a compact, read-only version of the team report — showing each Pokémon's sprite, build, and the author's strategy notes — without needing the viewer to visit the site separately.

Embeds are responsive and load asynchronously so they don't slow down the host page. The embed URL follows the pattern `https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/embed/[id]`.

For Discord, the `/s/[id]` link automatically generates a rich Open Graph preview showing the team's Pokémon and a summary — no embed code needed.

## Key concepts glossary

- **Team report:** A structured document covering a VGC team's six Pokémon builds (moves, item, EVs/IVs, nature, tera type), overall team strategy, matchup plans against common threats, damage calculations, and speed tier comparisons.
- **Regulation set / Format:** VGC rotates its legal Pokémon list seasonally. Regulation G and Regulation H are standard formats from the Scarlet & Violet era. Regulations M-A and M-B (Pokémon Champions) are the 2026 formats that add Mega Evolutions and replace EVs with SP. M-B is a superset of M-A and is the current, Worlds-2026 format.
- **SP (Stat Points):** The Champions stat-training budget — 66 total per Pokémon, 32 maximum per stat. Not the same as EVs and not convertible 1:1 to them.
- **Restricted Legendary:** High-power Legendary Pokémon that are legal in limited quantities per team — a maximum of two in Regulations G, H, M-A and M-B.
- **Speed tier:** A comparison of a Pokémon's Speed stat relative to common threats to determine who moves first without Trick Room or priority moves.
- **Damage calc / Calculation:** A computation of how much damage a specific move deals from one Pokémon to another under specific conditions (EVs, stat boosts, weather, terrain, etc.). Essential for EV spread decisions.
- **Matchup plan:** Notes on how a team handles specific opposing team archetypes — what lead to use, what to bring, what to watch out for.
- **PokePaste import:** Reports can be seeded from Pokémon Showdown team format text or a pokepast.es URL. The importer parses species, moves, items, abilities, EVs, IVs, natures, and tera types automatically.

VGC Team Report is an independent tool for the competitive Pokémon community. It is not affiliated with The Pokémon Company International, Nintendo, or Game Freak.
